note: Families of everyday objects in which cameras have been sold or documented. Alphabetical by id, never ranked by frequency: there are no reliable statistics on what is found in rentals. Vendor claims are vendor claims, not independently verified performance. Illustrations are generic drawings, never photos of a product.

families.name: Air freshener
observable: A small round opening or a dark window on the face, that a spray nozzle or a light sensor does not explain
Placed or turned toward a bed, a shower or a toilet rather than toward the room
No refill slot, or a refill that cannot be removed
A model reference that does not match a known air-freshener brand
lookalikes: Automatic dispensers with a motion or light sensor window
Plug-in diffusers with a status LED
checks: Read the brand and reference on the back or the base and compare them with the maker's page
Look at the opening at an angle with a light: does it go through, or is it a printed dot?
Note where it points; ask the host what it is
families.limits: Battery models record to a card with no network: invisible to network and Bluetooth scans.

families.name: Alarm clock
observable: A pinhole or a small dark circle in the display window or the frame, apart from the digits
A display that is darker in one spot, as if something sits behind it
Turned toward the bed when the bedside table would be the natural place
lookalikes: Clocks with a light sensor for automatic brightness
Clocks with an IR receiver for a remote
checks: Compare the reference on the base with the maker's page and photos
Shine a light at an angle on the display: a lens behind tinted plastic can reflect as a small circle
Note the orientation
families.limits: A clock on mains power can record continuously to a card without any network.

families.name: Clock radio
observable: A small opening in the speaker grille or the display window that the radio does not need
A grille that is more transparent in one spot
No working radio tuner, or a remote with buttons the clock does not use
lookalikes: Clock radios with a light sensor or an IR receiver
Speakers with a status LED behind the grille
checks: Compare the reference with the maker's page
Look through the grille at an angle with a light
Note the orientation
families.limits: Mains powered: can record all the time to a card, with no network at all.

families.name: Coat hook
observable: A hook thicker than an ordinary one, with a flat front face
A small round opening on the face, at the height of a person
A hook placed on the inside of a bathroom or toilet door, facing the room
lookalikes: Ordinary hooks with a decorative screw cap
Adhesive hooks with a round logo
checks: Look at the face with a light at an angle
Compare with an ordinary hook of the same set, if there are several
Note the orientation and the height
families.limits: Usually battery and card: no network, nothing for a scan to see.

families.name: Eyeglasses
observable: A small round opening at the bridge or at a hinge
Temples thicker than usual, a charging contact or port
Worn by someone, not left in a room: this family concerns a person, not a place
lookalikes: Ordinary frames with decorative rivets
Smart glasses sold openly with a camera and a recording light
checks: Look for a charging port or contacts on a temple
Look at the bridge and hinges with a light
families.limits: Smart glasses may advertise over Bluetooth, but an unidentified Bluetooth device is not a camera.

families.name: Key fob / remote
observable: A car-key or remote shape with no vehicle or device it belongs to
A small opening at one end, a USB port under a cap
Buttons that do nothing visible
lookalikes: Real car keys and garage remotes
USB flash drives shaped like keys
checks: Ask what it opens
If it has a USB port and you are allowed to, look at its interfaces with the USB tool on a computer you trust
families.limits: On USB it may show only a storage interface, or nothing until it is switched on.

families.name: Miniature camera module
observable: A small bare board with a lens, often taped or hidden inside another object
A thin cable leading to a battery or a USB supply where no device needs one
A lens a few millimetres wide pointing through a hole in furniture, a vent or a ceiling tile
lookalikes: Smoke and motion sensor parts
Wi-Fi repeaters and smart-home hubs with a status LED
checks: Follow unexplained cables to where they lead (without opening mains devices)
Look at holes that point toward private spaces
Note what you see and where
families.limits: Bare modules are what every other family hides: Wi-Fi modules may appear on the network; card-only modules never do.

families.name: Pen
observable: A small hole in the clip or above the clip
A pen heavier or thicker than usual that unscrews to a USB plug
lookalikes: Ordinary pens with a decorative clip ring
Stylus pens and USB-drive pens
checks: Look at the clip with a light
If it unscrews to USB and you are allowed to, look at its interfaces with the USB tool
families.limits: Card only, no network. On USB it often shows as storage only.

families.name: Telephone wall jack
observable: A jack in a place where no phone line makes sense, or a newer plate than the others
A small opening on the plate, besides the socket itself
A jack with no cable plugged in, placed facing a bed
lookalikes: Ordinary telephone and network wall plates
Plates with a screw cap or a label hole
checks: Compare with other plates in the building
Look at the plate with a light at an angle
Do not unscrew wall plates: ask the host
families.limits: Wired into the wall: may record to a card with no network presence.

families.name: Picture frame
observable: A small hole in the frame or the mat that the picture does not explain
A frame much thicker or heavier than its size needs
A cable or a charging port on a frame that is not a digital frame
lookalikes: Digital photo frames (with a screen, Wi-Fi and a power cable)
Frames with a hanging hole or a decorative stud
checks: Look at the frame and the mat with a light at an angle
Note the orientation
Compare with the other frames in the room
families.limits: Battery and card versions have no network.

families.name: Power bank
observable: A small opening on the face or an edge, apart from the ports and the charge LEDs
A power bank left in place, pointed at a bed, not charging anything
No brand or capacity marking, or markings that do not match a known product
lookalikes: Ordinary power banks with a flashlight LED
Power banks with a charge-level display
checks: Read the markings and compare them with the maker's page
Look at the face with a light at an angle
Note the orientation
families.limits: On USB it usually shows no data interface at all: an empty USB result excludes nothing.

families.name: Power strip
observable: A small opening at the end or near the switch, apart from the sockets and the LED
A strip placed facing a bed or a shower, with nothing plugged in
lookalikes: Strips with a lit switch or a surge-protection LED
Smart strips (Wi-Fi) sold openly
checks: Look at the end and the switch with a light
Note the orientation
Never open a mains device
families.limits: Mains powered: may record continuously to a card. Smart strips appear on the network for reasons that have nothing to do with a camera.

families.name: Smoke detector
observable: A detector in an unusual place (in a bathroom, low on a wall) or more than one in a small room
A small dark circle on the face apart from the test button and the LED
A detector with no test button or no certification marks
lookalikes: Real smoke, heat or CO detectors (they have an LED and a test button)
Motion sensors of an alarm system
checks: Look at the face with a light from the side
Read the markings if you can see them from below
Do not remove or open safety detectors: ask the host
families.limits: A real detector must not be taken down to check it. Card-only models are invisible to scans.

families.name: Tissue box
observable: A small hole in the print of the box, often in a dark part of the pattern
A box that is heavy, rigid or that you cannot open at the bottom
A box that stays full
lookalikes: Ordinary tissue boxes (printed patterns can look like dots)
checks: Lift it: weight and rigidity
Look at dark parts of the print with a light
Note the orientation

families.name: USB charger
observable: A small round opening or a dark window on a face, that a charge LED does not explain
A charger plugged in facing a bed or a shower with nothing connected to it
Heavier or deeper than a charger of that power
No brand, no certification marks, or a reference that searches to a camera
lookalikes: Ordinary chargers with a charge LED
Smart plugs and night lights
checks: Read the reference and marks on the side and compare them with the maker's page
Look at the face with a light at an angle: a lens reflects as a small round spot
Note the orientation; unplug it only if you are allowed to and it is not damaged
families.limits: A charger has no USB data interface: plugging it into a computer shows nothing, and that excludes nothing.

families.name: Wall outlet / plug adapter
observable: A travel adapter or socket plate with a small opening between or beside the sockets
A plate newer or deeper than the others in the room
An adapter left plugged in with nothing on it, facing a bed
lookalikes: Ordinary adapters, child-safety covers, USB wall sockets
Night lights and smart plugs
checks: Compare with the other sockets of the room
Look at the face with a light at an angle
Never unscrew a socket: ask the host
families.limits: Wired to the mains: may record continuously, with no network at all.

references.title: Sneaky Spy Devices and Defective Detectors: The Ecosystem of Intimate Partner Surveillance with Covert Devices
references.use: Covert devices sold to consumers, and detectors that fail to find them: why a scan is never a guarantee.

references.title: Lumos: Identifying and Localizing Diverse Hidden IoT Devices in an Unfamiliar Environment
references.use: Research on finding Wi-Fi devices by their traffic. Hardware Dog does not capture traffic: it asks devices what they announce.

references.title: Usability Determines Safety for At-Risk Users
references.use: Reference given for this module, not yet reviewed here.

references.title: LAPD: Hidden Spy Camera Detection using Smartphone Time-of-Flight Sensors
references.use: Works only with specific phones that expose a ToF sensor. Not integrated: a browser cannot use it.
